findings.where: the fling itself — per_frame[] of scroll_webkit.json, the 802 frames the framework reported during the scene that produced this clip
findings.what: In the run that made this clip the app needed 49.5 s of build time to draw the 300 frames that are 4.80 s of app time (10.3x real time): 67 of those 300 frames cost over 400 ms to build, median heavy frame 662 ms, worst 1977 ms; across the whole 802-frame record 182 frames exceed 400 ms, they recur every 3 to 7 frames (median gap 5), and 131.6 s of the record's 136.9 s of total build time is spent inside them. The log's own header says build_ms 'is the framework laying out and painting: the app's own work, and comparable between runs', so this is not the container's missing GPU (raster_ms, which is the machine, sits at p50 118 ms and never exceeds 191 ms). The published clip cannot show it: each frame is grabbed one at a time with the clock stepped, so the mp4 plays perfectly smooth — I stepped all 300 frames and the mean absolute change never drops below 17.5 grey levels, there is not one held frame, and 11_chat_scroll.fling.json records max |asked - moved| = 0.0000 over all 300 ticks. The cost is visible only in the timing log, and there it is unambiguous. The heavy frames track the link's polling: this run records 187 sync rounds in 802 frames (one every 4.29) against 182 heavy frames (one every 4.40), and it carries a fault the other runs do not — 11_chat_scroll.report.json sync.faults 1, last_fault '401 the signature does not match'.
findings.why: The row forbids 'scroll jank against the year-deep seeded history' by name. At 10.3x real time a 4.8-second flick through the thread costs the phone 49 seconds of layout; the thread would freeze for two thirds of a second every few frames, every few frames, for as long as the scroll lasts. That is the single thing most certain to send either person back to Instagram, and it is the reason the category cannot exceed its floor.

findings.where: the top of the list, between the standing-line header and the first sheet — and, for taking a message back, the whole set
findings.what: Two of the eleven capabilities the row enumerates cannot be seen anywhere. Editing: 13_messenger_states.report.json names one edited row (0001MCJ1M0TM1AH3BRGTH8Q39P, folded_in.message_edit 1, clipped_at_an_edge 0.217) but that row is not drawn. I measured it: the header's paper ends at y=201 px and the first sheet's torn fringe begins at y=285 px, and every scanline from y=205 to y=284 has a maximum luma of 116 with zero pixels above 170 — bare desk. Fitting rows 8071-8075 (tops 28, 226, 306, 428, 581 logical) against the five measured paper bands (px 331-806, 873-1079, 1125-1425, 1492-1882, 1953-2202) puts the list origin at logical y=58, so row 8070's box ends at px 258 and its paper, at the 58-64% paper-to-gutter ratio the five whole sheets measure, ends around px 180 — behind the opaque header. None of the five sheets that are on the glass carries an 'edited' mark. Deleting: taken_back is [] and folded_in.message_delete is 0 in all seven region reports that carry those fields (02, 06, 10, 11_alternates, 11_chat_scroll, 11_plain, 13). tests.log line 118 names a test 'a note taken back does not say how far it got' and reliability.json reports delete ok ('the row became a stub on the host'), so the capability exists — but no artifact shows what an edited or a withdrawn note looks like to the person reading it.
findings.why: The row requires that every messenger capability is present and dependable and names editing and deleting among them; a capability whose appearance is never photographed is a capability the couple cannot be shown to have, and 13_messenger_states.png is the one artifact whose whole job is to show the states.

findings.where: the media lens, lower half of the masonry — three tiles at (x=494,y=2144,452x594), (x=965,y=2162,452x337) and (x=24,y=2615,451x328), plus the tile at (x=24,y=2320,450x273)
findings.what: Three tiles in the photograph grid are entirely blank paper: inside each, after a 12 px inset, not one pixel is darker than luma 120 and not one is between 120 and 170 — no picture, no caption, no author, no date, nothing. A fourth carries only a play mark and '0:03' with no poster frame and no author line, while every loaded tile carries either a photograph or a waveform plus 'author · date'. This is not a load in progress: 04_moments.report.json records tiles_built 52, tiles_without_a_picture 8, and blobs {asked 18, arrived 18, reading 0, waiting 0} — every blob that was asked for arrived and nothing is outstanding. The shutter fired 2400 ms after the lens changed plus a 900 ms settle. The same measurement over the other two lenses finds no blank tile at all (crops/04_moments_what_happened.png: 7 tiles, 0 blank; crops/04_moments_what_we_felt.png: 1 tile, 0 blank), so it is the photographs specifically that come up empty.
findings.why: The row asks for dependable photos and media search; a year of Moments in which roughly one tile in six is a blank sheet, with no word about why and no way to ask for it again, is exactly the reason to go back to the app that still has the picture — and the thread itself proves the app knows how to do better, since 13_messenger_states.png says 'it would not go', gives the reason in plain words and offers 'send it again'.

findings.where: the banner in the lower right of the crop; the note at the foot of reception.json
findings.what: Nothing in the set shows either phone being told a message arrived while the app is closed on the platform this messenger has to run on. What is shown is a desktop Chromium banner on a Linux virtual display reading '127.0.0.1:8796 · now / noor / wrote something', and the record says so itself: browser 'chromium', app_open false, and the closing note — 'this is not an iPhone banner, there is no lock screen in evidence, and what an installed iOS web app does with the same call is not shown anywhere in this build.' pwa.json confirms the page offers a standalone manifest and a service worker but reads display_mode_standalone false, i.e. it was read in a tab, not from the home screen, which is the only place iOS grants the push API.
findings.why: The reason given is a real standing limit of the harness rather than an excuse, and the record is admirably honest about it — but the consequence is untouched: a messenger that cannot be shown to tell you a message has arrived is one you check by opening the other app, and the row is decided by whether either person has a reason to do that.

findings.where: the file timestamps against MANIFEST.json's checks list
findings.what: The numbers that say the scroll is cheap belong to no artifact in the set. These five records were written 2026-09-11 between 16:59 and 17:08; MANIFEST.json was written 2026-09-10T19:16Z and its checks list does not contain one of them. In them the same fling costs 2.47 s and 2.38 s of build for the same 4.80 s of app time (0.5x real time), with zero frames over 400 ms and a worst frame of 77 ms and 76 ms, against 49.5 s and 1977 ms in the run that produced the clip; their sync records show 22 rounds against 187. what_the_alternates_cost.json says plainly that both arms were built fresh 'because a capture taken before this commit differs by more than the fonts'. So the fast build exists and produced no still and no clip that is in this set.
findings.why: A critic judges the artifacts, and the artifact's own record is the slow one; a measurement taken on a build that shipped no picture cannot stand in for the picture, and saying which run a number belongs to is the difference between a fix and a claim.

findings.where: the composer block, first line — against view.partner_typing in the report
findings.what: The glass says 'noor writing…' at the top of the composer sheet (I read it at full resolution, px 2317-2888). The report for that same frame records view.partner_typing false, and declares read_at 'the shutter'. The scene log shows awaitView partner_typing true succeeded before slowSend, so the flag was true earlier in the scene and false by the time the report was written.
findings.why: Typing indication is one of the capabilities the row names and it is on the glass and legible, which is what matters — but the record of the picture disagrees with the picture about that exact field while claiming to have been read at the shutter, which makes every other 'read_at: the shutter' field one degree less checkable.

findings.where: the transport bar, the readout at its right end
findings.what: It reads '0:00 / 0:03' while 14_media_viewer.report.json records video position_ms 625 of duration_ms 2500. The duration rounds 2.5 s up to 3 s while the elapsed floors 0.625 s down to 0, so the two ends of one readout round opposite ways and the playhead can never reach the time the same readout states. The knob itself is honest: I measured it at 21% of the track against the 25% the report records.
findings.why: Small, but the row is decided on whether a marker can be trusted, and a duration that is half a second longer than the film is a number the couple would learn to ignore.

findings.what: 'Correct ordering after going offline and reconnecting' is evidenced only by a headless harness on transport 'local' at 127.0.0.1 — 26 events queued offline and all delivered, seq 1..175 gapless and monotonic after the gap, 0 duplicates, same_order_both_sides true, with five faults actually injected (lose-response, offline, online, offline, online). No still and no clip shows a reconnect. The one run over the real transport, coldstart.json, is dated 2026-09-05 with distinct node keys and four events in the same order on both sides, and its later_check is 'pending' because 'the nodes were not answering when this was re-run'; reliability.json's tailscale block says the same.
findings.why: The measurement is detailed, fault-injected and convincing on its own terms, and I count it — but the row's ordering clause is the one thing no picture in the set touches, and the only run over the wire the mission actually names is five days older than the capture and could not be repeated on the day.

what_is_working: The delivery ladder is legible in ink and never a spinner: 'going ⫼' while it is on its way, 'sent ✓' when it has gone, 'read ✓✓' when it has been read (02_chat.png, three of them, at 08:20, 08:23 and 08:25), and 'it would not go ✕' in red when it has not. There is no rotating spinner anywhere in the set; every waiting state is a word.

The refusal row in 13_messenger_states.png is the best thing in the evidence: 'Thu 3 Sep · 19:40  it would not go ✕ / send it again / this phone is on an older version and cannot read that' — the state, a retry, and the actual reason in the couple's own language, all inside the sheet.

The reply in 13_messenger_states.png quotes the original in grey behind a vertical rule with the answer beneath it, and the composer carries the reply bar with a cancel ('↵ answering leaving now. dont cut the end … ✕') — reply is shown from both ends, being written and having been sent.
Typing indication is on the glass and in words: 'noor writing…' at the head of the composer in 13_messenger_states.png, and held through every frame of 06_unfolding.mp4 and 11_chat_scroll.mp4.

Search is real: 12_search.png shows the query 'morning' with a clear, fifteen facets including PHOTOGRAPHS, VIDEO, TALKING, FEELINGS and THIS YEAR, and four results in descending date order (Wed 6 May, Thu 26 Mar, Sat 24 Jan, Tue 16 Dec), each with a thumbnail and the matched word highlighted in the line; 12_search.report.json records 6 hits against 14,062 events, and reliability.json shows nine queries each answered by an event of the type asked for.

Voice notes and photographs read as themselves: a play triangle, a waveform and '0:51' with 'Thu 26 Mar · 08:23 read ✓✓' beneath it (02_chat.png), and a reaction that is a torn scrap with a drawn ring rather than an emoji.

The scroll offset never stalls or drifts: over all 300 ticks of 11_chat_scroll.fling.json the thread moved exactly what it was asked to move (max |asked - moved| = 0.0000), no tick moved under a third of a logical pixel, and stepping the clip myself I found no repeated frame and a per-frame mean change between 17.5 and 38.2 grey levels. Six consecutive frames (38-43) are each fully painted — sheets, handwriting, timestamps, read marks, reactions — with no placeholder and no tearing.

Ordering holds where I could check it on the glass: 02_chat.png runs 08:20, 08:23, 08:25, 08:28, 08:40, 08:44, 08:55; 08_state_propagating.mp4 runs 20:48, 21:00, 21:03 (I read the timestamps at full resolution rather than off the strip); 06_unfolding.mp4 lands two notes in time order, 19:49 then 19:54, with no duplicate row.

Warm launch with the whole year present is quick: every store:kept scene reaches its first frame in 1.15-1.39 s (02_chat 1310 ms, of which 696 ms is the log). The 8-14.6 s figures in 01_pulse, dusk_pulse, 11_plain and 11_alternates are fresh profiles importing the seeded year, not a path a person walks; the genuine empty first run, 10_first_run.json, is 694 ms.

The empty state is written with restraint: 'nothing from them yet. the six words are on the other phone.' and 'first one's yours. whatever it is. it only goes to one person.' — no badge, no exclamation mark, nobody called a user.

reliability.json exercises twenty-one capabilities with faults actually injected and reports 177 events on both sides, 0 duplicates, same order both sides, a kill mid-send that did not duplicate, a draft and pairing intact across a process restart, and a refusal held out of the wire for a round and delivered as seq 176 when asked again.
verdict: The messenger is nearly all here and much of it is better than the thing it is replacing: the delivery ladder is four legible rungs of ink with no spinner anywhere in the set, the refusal row states its reason and offers a retry, reply and typing are photographed from both ends, search reaches into a 14,062-event year with fifteen facets and highlights the hit, and the fling never drops or duplicates a row. What holds the row below its floor is not any of that but the one number the clip cannot show. 11_chat_scroll.mp4 is assembled a frame at a time with the app's clock stepped, so it plays smooth by construction — and its own timing record, evidence/logs/scroll_webkit.json, says the app spent 49.5 s of build work to produce the 4.80 s of app time in it: 67 of 300 frames over 400 ms, a heavy frame every three to seven frames, worst 1977 ms, with 96% of all the build time in the record inside those frames, and the log itself insists build_ms is the app's own work and not this machine's missing GPU. On a phone that thread cannot be scrolled, and that is the row's named failure; it is marked blocking and it is the finding keeping the category at or below 26. Three things make it worse rather than better: the reassuring counter-numbers (0.5x real time, no frame over 77 ms) were written a day after MANIFEST.json and belong to builds that shipped no picture here, so the fix exists but the artifact does not; a sixth of the Moments grid is blank paper with nothing said about it, in an app that elsewhere knows how to say 'it would not go, send it again'; and two capabilities the row enumerates by name, editing and deleting, cannot be seen in any frame — the one edited row the evidence claims sits above the top of its own still, measured as eighty pixels of bare desk where it should be.

not_worth_opening.why: the pulse region carries no messenger surface; its report shows no delivery state, no composer and no thread rows, only state and feeling counts. I read the report and the load record instead.
the shared-life modules, not the thread; its report has an empty delivery map and no composer.

settings; its report carries no delivery, no rows and no composer. The one settings fact my row wanted — what each kind of arrival is allowed to do — I took from logs/reception.json's prefs block instead.
a 300% crop of a torn paper edge for the material row; at that magnification there is no delivery marker, composer or row state in frame.
a 300% crop of handwriting for the material row; it answers whether the hand repeats itself, not whether a message arrived.
a 300% crop of the contact shadow under a sheet; nothing in it bears on delivery, ordering or state.

the second lighting condition of the pulse page. It would matter to my row if it showed the thread — a read mark that disappears at dusk would be a finding — but it is the pulse region, which has no delivery markers in it at all; its report confirms an empty delivery map.

vibration patterns for the feeling row. I read logs/haptics.check.json for the summary and noted in passing that no region report in the set carries the asked_a_motor_for record the briefing describes, but the motor is not a messenger capability and I leave the finding to whoever owns that row.

further frames of the same Chromium-on-Linux reception scene, which logs/reception.json states is not an artifact and not an iPhone. One banner was enough to establish what the scene does and does not show; the record's own note carries the rest.

not_worth_opening.path: evidence/logs/hand.json, fonts.json, surfaces.json, grain.json, holes.json, lines.json, tears.json, torn.json, flat.json, hairline.json
not_worth_opening.why: measurements of paper, ink, ruling, tears and flatness for the material and typography rows. None of them records a message, a state, an order or a cost.
the audio of the feeling clips; sound is not one of the capabilities this row enumerates.
the full pattern table, the crop recipes and the asset manifests — capture bookkeeping and feeling-row material, with nothing about delivery, ordering or the thread.
another reader's conclusions rather than evidence; the briefing forbids them and I left them closed.
